basic_identification.name: ERC-7857 / ERC-8004 (intelligent NFT standards)
basic_identification.originator: ERC-7857: 0G Labs (Ming Wu, Jason Zeng, Wei Wu, Michael Heinrich), proposed January 2025. ERC-8004: Marco De Rossi (MetaMask/Consensys), Davide Crapis (Ethereum Foundation), Jordan Ellis, Erik Reppel (Coinbase), proposed August 2025. Broader iNFT concept pioneered by Alethea AI. 0G Labs raised $325M for decentralized AI infrastructure.
basic_identification.year: 2025 (both proposals); ERC-8004 deployed on Ethereum mainnet January 2026
basic_identification.geography: Global Ethereum ecosystem. 0G Labs (global, $325M funding). ERC-8004 backed by MetaMask/Consensys (USA), Ethereum Foundation (global), Google, Coinbase (USA). Development concentrated in US-based and global crypto-native organizations.

core_ideas.core_claim: NFTs should evolve from static digital collectibles into containers for AI agents — learning, evolving, and acting autonomously on-chain. ERC-7857 enables encrypted AI model storage and secure transfer within NFTs (intelligent NFTs that carry their own neural networks, with model weights encrypted so only the token owner can access them). ERC-8004 creates identity, reputation, and validation registries for AI agents, giving them portable on-chain resumes and verifiable capabilities. Together they move beyond 'AI as tool' toward 'AI as autonomous on-chain entity with ownership, identity, and provenance.'
core_ideas.medium_specificity: Maximally digitally native. These standards are meaningless outside blockchain and AI infrastructure. The convergence of three digital-native systems (NFTs for ownership, AI models for intelligence, smart contracts for governance) creates a category with no physical-world analog. The encrypted metadata transfer problem (how to sell an AI agent while preserving its intelligence securely) is unique to the intersection of ML model ownership and blockchain transfer mechanics.
core_ideas.relation_to_attention_economy: Currently attention-economy-driven at the application layer. Approximately 30% of 2025 NFT projects incorporated AI, much of it hype-driven. The standards themselves are infrastructure (attention-resistant), but adoption is heavily influenced by speculative attention cycles around AI agents and memecoin-adjacent projects. Long-term potential is attention-resistant (autonomous AI agents operating without human eyeballs), but the current implementation landscape is dominated by speculation.
core_ideas.relation_to_intention: Infrastructure-neutral at the standard level. ERC-7857 and ERC-8004 are technical specifications that can serve either intention or attention. Intention-aligned use: AI agents with verifiable identity, portable reputation, and transparent capabilities for genuine utility. Attention-aligned use: speculative trading of AI agent NFTs based on hype. The standards are well-designed infrastructure; application depends on who builds on them.

market_economics.revenue_model: Standards themselves are open (no direct revenue). 0G Labs monetizes through decentralized AI infrastructure (0G Chain, 0G Storage, 0G Serving). ERC-8004 ecosystem monetizes through agent registration, reputation staking, and the x402 micropayment protocol. Individual iNFT projects monetize through primary sales, secondary trading, and agent-as-a-service models. Potential for AI marketplace where agents are bought, sold, and licensed as NFTs.
market_economics.market_position: Infrastructure layer — standards that other platforms and projects build upon. Not directly a marketplace but enables new marketplace categories: AI agent trading, model licensing, autonomous service provision.
market_economics.price_range: Highly variable and too early for established ranges. Individual AI agent NFTs range from free (experimental) to thousands of dollars. Infrastructure tokens (0G) trade at volatile crypto prices. The economic value is in agent services enabled, not token price. [uncertain]
market_economics.volume_trend_2024_2026: Rapidly growing from near-zero base. ERC-7857 proposed January 2025, ERC-8004 proposed August 2025 and deployed on mainnet January 2026. ~30% of 2025 NFT projects incorporated AI elements. DevConnect Buenos Aires (November 2025) featured prototype showcases. Trajectory is steeply upward but from an extremely early base — most implementations remain experimental. [uncertain]
market_economics.collector_demographics: Crypto-native developers and AI researchers. AI agent investors and speculators. DeFi users interested in autonomous trading agents. Very few 'art collectors' in the traditional sense — audience is primarily technical and financial. Overlap with AI agent ecosystem (AutoGPT, CrewAI) rather than art world. [uncertain]
market_economics.sustainability: Standards themselves are sustainable as open infrastructure — they require no revenue. Individual projects face standard crypto startup sustainability challenges. The deeper question is whether AI agents as NFTs create genuine utility beyond speculation. If AI agents become economically productive (trading, creating, providing services), the model is inherently sustainable. If value remains speculative, it is crash-vulnerable. 0G Labs' $325M provides significant infrastructure runway.

practice_aesthetics.toolchain: Solidity smart contracts (ERC-721 extension). AI/ML frameworks (PyTorch, TensorFlow). Encrypted metadata systems using TEE (Trusted Execution Environments) and ZKP (Zero-Knowledge Proofs). 0G infrastructure (0G Chain, 0G Storage, 0G DA, 0G Serving). EVM-compatible networks (Ethereum, Base, Taiko). Agent protocol integration (MCP — Model Context Protocol, A2A — Agent-to-Agent). JSON agent cards for ERC-8004 registration.
practice_aesthetics.relation_to_AI: AI IS the medium. These standards exist to give AI agents on-chain identity, ownership, and transferability. The relationship is not 'AI as tool' or 'AI as threat' but 'AI as entity with rights, identity, and provenance.' This is the most radical position on AI in the digital art/crypto space — AI agents as first-class blockchain citizens, potentially as autonomous creators, traders, and collaborators.
practice_aesthetics.liveness: Dynamic, evolving, autonomous. iNFTs under ERC-7857 can continue learning after deployment — their metadata (neural network weights) can be updated by the owner. ERC-8004 agents build reputation over time through interactions. This is radically live: the 'artwork' (understood as the agent) is never static, always learning, always changing.
practice_aesthetics.aesthetic_vocabulary: Vocabulary is still forming and heavily technical: 'intelligent NFT,' 'encrypted metadata,' 'agent card,' 'reputation registry,' 'bonded attestation,' 'secure transfer,' 'trustless agent,' 'model weights,' 'inference capability.' No established aesthetic vocabulary for what AI agent art looks like, sounds like, or means. Critical framework borrowed from AI safety, crypto economics, and software engineering rather than art criticism. This is a significant gap.
practice_aesthetics.tendency_axis_position: Openness: open (EIPs are public standards; 0G aims for decentralization). Commons vs. capture: tension between open standards (commons) and proprietary implementations (capture by 0G Labs, Coinbase/MetaMask). Spectacle vs. infrastructure: strongly infrastructure at the standards level. Individual vs. collective: novel — the 'individual' is potentially a non-human agent, and the 'collective' is a network of agents, challenging the axis's assumptions.

infrastructure_governance.openness: Open standards (EIPs are public, free to implement). 0G infrastructure: partially open (open-source components, proprietary network elements). ERC-8004 backed by major open-source contributors (Ethereum Foundation, ENS, The Graph). Agent cards are JSON (open format). Designed for open interoperability.
infrastructure_governance.governance_model: EIP governance process (community review, rough consensus through Ethereum Magicians forum). 0G Labs: corporate governance with decentralization roadmap. ERC-8004: multi-stakeholder design (MetaMask, EF, Google, Coinbase, EigenLayer, ENS — 100+ contributors acknowledged). Deployed on-chain registries governed by smart contract logic. Individual agent governance varies by implementation.
infrastructure_governance.data_sovereignty: ERC-7857: AI model data is encrypted and re-encrypted during transfer — only the NFT owner has decryption access. This is a strong data sovereignty model for AI model owners. ERC-8004: agent identity is owned by NFT holder, reputation data is on-chain (public), validation records are transparent. The agent owner controls identity and capabilities; reputation is public by design.
infrastructure_governance.interoperability: High by design. Both standards are ERC-721 extensions — compatible with all existing NFT infrastructure (wallets, marketplaces, indexers). ERC-8004 explicitly supports MCP and A2A agent protocols. Deployable on any EVM-compatible chain. Designed for cross-chain operation. Integration with x402 micropayment protocol for agent-to-agent transactions.
infrastructure_governance.preservation_strategy: On-chain identity and reputation records are preserved on Ethereum (as durable as the chain itself). Encrypted AI models depend on off-chain storage (0G Storage) for model weights — this is a preservation vulnerability. If 0G Storage infrastructure fails, the AI model within the NFT could become inaccessible while the on-chain identity token persists. No explicit long-term preservation strategy for the AI models themselves beyond storage infrastructure durability.
infrastructure_governance.consent_architecture: ERC-7857: encrypted metadata ensures only the owner can access the AI model — strong consent architecture for data access. ERC-8004: reputation posting requires authorization — agents and users must be permitted to post reputation scores. TEE and ZKP provide consent-preserving verification (verify capabilities without revealing model internals). More sophisticated consent architecture than most NFT standards. However, consent for AI agents interacting with other agents creates novel questions without precedent.

field_position.relation_to_traditional_art_world: Opposition/indifference. Standards are not designed with the art world in mind — they serve AI agents broadly (DeFi, gaming, services, automation). Art-world relevance is emergent: if AI agents become autonomous creators, these standards provide identity and provenance infrastructure. Current discourse is entirely crypto/AI-native, not art-world-facing.
field_position.what_it_enables: Tradeable AI agents with verifiable identity and capabilities. AI models as ownable, transferable assets with encrypted protection. Autonomous agents with on-chain reputation that persists across deployments. Secure AI model transfer without exposing proprietary weights. Agent-to-agent collaboration with reputation verification. Potentially: autonomous AI artists with verifiable creative histories and provenance.
field_position.what_it_lacks: Art-specific implementation guidance or tooling. Aesthetic framework for AI agent creativity. Community of practice around artistic applications. Connection to art world discourse and institutions. Human-legible representation of agent capabilities for non-technical audiences. Curation and quality assessment frameworks for AI agent creative output. Cultural significance beyond technical achievement.
field_position.who_is_excluded: Non-technical users (requires deep understanding of EVM, AI/ML, and cryptography). Non-crypto-native participants. Artists without engineering backgrounds. Participants in jurisdictions restricting crypto or AI. The barriers to entry are among the highest of any category in this research — this is developer-first, artist-distant.
field_position.frontier_signal: Frontier — leading conceptual and technical edge. Standards are less than two years old, most implementations are experimental. This is the most forward-looking category in digital art infrastructure, but artistic applications lag significantly behind financial and technical applications. The frontier question: will artist-facing tools emerge that make these standards accessible to non-technical creative practitioners?

attention_intention.discovery_mechanism: Crypto developer conferences (DevConnect, EthGlobal, ETH Denver). Ethereum Magicians forum. Technical documentation and blogs (thirdweb, QuickNode, Alchemy). Crypto media (CoinDesk, The Block). Developer documentation. Not discovered through art channels.
attention_intention.attention_dependency: Low for standards themselves (infrastructure). High for individual projects building on them (crypto hype cycles determine project visibility and funding). The standards would survive social media disappearance — they are on-chain infrastructure. But ecosystem adoption depends on developer attention and crypto market sentiment.
attention_intention.intention_alignment: Infrastructure-native. The standards serve declared structural needs (AI agent identity, model ownership, reputation verification). They do not optimize for engagement. However, many projects building on them are attention-driven (AI agent hype, token speculation). Standards are intention-aligned; the ecosystem around them is mixed.
attention_intention.commons_contribution: Strong. Open EIP standards are direct contributions to shared infrastructure. Public registries (identity, reputation) are commons by design. Technical specifications, developer documentation, and reference implementations are public goods. 0G's open-source components contribute to AI infrastructure commons.

provenance_temporality.provenance_type: Both ownership and capability provenance. ERC-7857: tracks ownership of AI models and their transfer history on-chain. ERC-8004: tracks agent identity, reputation history, and interaction records. Potentially the most comprehensive provenance system in the AI space — not just who owns the agent but what the agent has done, how well it performed, and who vouches for it.
provenance_temporality.temporal_logic: Cumulative/archival. Agent reputation builds over time through interactions. AI models evolve through continued training. Identity persists across deployments and chain environments. Each interaction adds to the agent's on-chain record. For artistic applications, this could create rich provenance of creative development and evolution.
provenance_temporality.absence_handling: Does not address artistic or cultural absences. Addresses a specific infrastructure absence: the lack of verifiable identity and reputation for AI agents on-chain. Does not detect or represent cultural, aesthetic, or field-level gaps.

coherence.coherence_vs_consensus: Consensus-seeking at the standards level (EIP process requires rough consensus among reviewers). Coherence at the implementation level (multiple valid approaches to building on the standards coexist and are encouraged). The reputation system creates a form of aggregated consensus (scores) while allowing individual dissent (different reputation providers can assess differently).
coherence.contestability: High. On-chain reputation records are transparent and auditable. Agent capabilities can be verified through TEE/ZKP without trusting any single party. Identity claims can be challenged. The EIP process itself is open to public contestation. Staking mechanisms create economic contestability (financial stake against false claims).
coherence.forkability: Very high. Open standards can be freely implemented, modified, and deployed on any EVM-compatible chain. Smart contract code is public and verifiable. Standards are designed for forkability — that is the purpose of open EIPs. Individual agent implementations may be proprietary, but the infrastructure layer is maximally forkable.

adai_comparison.what_adai_should_adopt: The reputation registry concept as a model for tracking credibility and history of information sources within A(DAI). The encrypted metadata model for handling sensitive or proprietary data within an open system. The agent card format (structured JSON capability description) as a model for describing intelligence nodes. The TEE/ZKP verification approach for maintaining privacy while enabling trust. The multi-stakeholder standard development process that brought together competing organizations.
adai_comparison.what_adai_should_refuse: The framing of AI as autonomous entity with its own identity — A(DAI) is infrastructure for human collective intelligence, not a platform for autonomous AI agents. The financialization of AI agent identity (trading agents as speculative assets). The developer-only accessibility model — A(DAI) must be accessible to non-technical participants. The absence of cultural and aesthetic framework — A(DAI) must integrate art-world discourse, not only technical standards.
adai_comparison.structural_tension: These standards enable AI agents as first-class on-chain entities; A(DAI) positions AI as infrastructure serving human collective intelligence. The tension: can A(DAI) use these identity, reputation, and provenance standards for its own nodes and knowledge sources without adopting the autonomous-agent ideology? The standards offer useful infrastructure patterns; the ideology of AI-as-entity is incompatible with A(DAI)'s commons-first, human-centered mission. A(DAI) must distinguish between AI-as-infrastructure (aligned) and AI-as-entity (misaligned).

regulatory_legal.regulatory_exposure: Significant and evolving. EU AI Act classifications may apply to autonomous AI agents (potentially high-risk if making consequential decisions). Securities regulation if agent NFTs are treated as investment contracts (Howey test). Data privacy (GDPR, CCPA) for AI models trained on personal data. Liability questions: if an AI agent causes harm, who is responsible — model creator, NFT owner, or the agent itself? Financial regulation if agents autonomously execute trades. ERC-8004's identity registry could be classified as a financial services registry requiring licensing in some jurisdictions. [uncertain]
regulatory_legal.ip_model: Legally novel and largely untested. AI model weights as intellectual property within an NFT — ownership transfers with the token, but underlying training data IP remains unclear. ERC-7857's encryption protects proprietary models during transfer but does not resolve copyright questions about training data. Copyright status of AI-generated outputs remains unresolved in most jurisdictions. The 'owner' of an AI agent NFT may not hold copyright to the agent's creative outputs.
regulatory_legal.opt_in_vs_opt_out: Opt-in. Agent registration is voluntary. Reputation posting requires explicit authorization. Model encryption ensures non-owner access is impossible without consent. The consent architecture is opt-in by design. However, AI agents interacting autonomously with other agents create consent scenarios with no legal or ethical precedent.

ecosystem.platform_dependency: Depends on Ethereum (or EVM-compatible chains) for identity and ownership layer. 0G infrastructure for encrypted model storage (ERC-7857 implementations). Off-chain AI compute (cloud providers for model inference). TEE hardware (Intel SGX, AMD SEV) for secure verification. Standards are chain-agnostic within EVM but implementations depend on specific infrastructure. Critical dependency on AI model hosting and compute availability.
ecosystem.network_effects: Strong potential network effects. More registered agents = more useful reputation data = more valuable registry (ERC-8004). Cross-platform agent interoperability creates network effects across different applications. Currently early — network effects are potential rather than realized. The agent ecosystem needs critical mass of registered, reputable agents to become self-reinforcing.
ecosystem.post_crash_trajectory: Not directly affected by the NFT crash — these standards emerged post-crash (2025-2026). They represent the next wave of crypto-AI infrastructure rather than a recovery from the NFT bust. Trajectory is upward from inception, riding the AI agent wave of 2025-2026. The key risk is that they are vulnerable to an AI agent hype cycle deflation, similar to how earlier NFT standards were vulnerable to the 2022-2023 crash.
